svg.title: TaskFlow API — technical architecture
svg.desc: Left to right: an HTTP client (curl, Postman) calls the TaskFlow API Spring Boot application on port 8080. Inside the application, TaskController routes CRUD requests to TaskService, which accesses an in-memory TaskRepository backed by a HashMap — volatile, no database. The summary endpoint computes statistics locally, builds a prompt, and calls the OpenRouter OpenAI-compatible chat model through Spring AI ChatClient; the model returns an unvalidated HTML fragment. Configuration comes from application.properties with dev and prod profiles, and the provider key is supplied through the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable. Lower panels document the REST API contract and known constraints.
svg.text: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 21 · Spring AI 2.0.0 · in-memory task store · OpenRouter free chat model
NTU AI Engineering · AIE-FT-03-Back End Development
TaskFlow API — Spring Boot app · single JVM · port :8080
application.properties — OpenRouter active; oMLX / Ollama alternatives commented out
Profiles — dev default (DEBUG logs) · prod (INFO) via SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
OPENAI_API_KEY — from environment (.env via shell / VS Code launch); required at
Build — Maven wrapper (JDK 21) → Spring Boot jar · run: ./mvnw spring-boot:run
Tests — ./mvnw clean test: context load + summary behaviour, mocked ChatClient
Storage — in-memory HashMap; all tasks lost on restart (no database)
Concurrency — per-method synchronized; compound find→modify→save not atomic
Auth — none on API endpoints; AI provider access key required at startup
AI output — unvalidated / unsanitised HTML; task titles sent to external provider

g.text: server assigns id; body id ignored
Task { id: long · title: string @NotBlank · completed: boolean }
Errors — 404 task missing · 400 blank title · 500 fallback (malformed JSON, non-numeric id, AI failure)
